Other German cities often use different lamp standards and less cobblestone around crossings.

These combined features suggest a quiet street edge of a large urban park in Berlin (e.g., streets flanking Tiergarten or local Kiez parks). Exact street is uncertain, but the elements narrow to Berlin park-adjacent residential streets rather than commercial boulevards.

features.geolocation_description: Blue square pedestrian crossing signs with a white triangle and zebra figure are standard German signage (Zeichen 350).
Circular blue disk with red slash (no parking) matches German sign conventions (single slash = no parking, X = no stopping).
Right-hand traffic with European-style dashed center line and zebra crosswalk width typical for Germany.
Granite cobblestone (Kleinpflaster) sidewalks and verge with beveled granite curbs are especially common in Berlin streetscapes.
Tall, curved arch streetlamp style frequently seen on Berlin residential/park-adjacent streets.
Park-edge context: benches set back from a cobbled verge and dense deciduous canopy is characteristic of Berlin’s inner-city parks and green corridors.
Duplicate pedestrian-crossing signs flanking a zebra at a calm one-lane-per-direction street with immediate park frontage narrows to specific residential park-edge streets in Berlin.
